identity.title: The SCUBA-2 Cosmology Legacy Survey: Multiwavelength Counterparts to 10<SUP>3</SUP> Submillimeter Galaxies in the UKIDSS-UDS Field

paper_type_evidence.quote: In this paper, we use these ALMA-detected SMGs as the training set to formulate our methodology to identify candidates counterpart for the rest of the SCUBA-2 SMG sample.

targets.name: SCUBA-2 sources in the UKIDSS-UDS field (30 ALMA-observed bright sources)

evidence.quote: We have carried out ALMA follow-up observations at 870 $\mu$m on 30 of the brighter SCUBA-2 sources in a Cycle-1 project 2012.1.00090.S

distance_source.value: photometric redshifts from eazy (Hartley et al. 2013)

evidence.quote: We have carried out ALMA follow-up observations at 870 $\mu$m on 30 of the brighter SCUBA-2 sources in a Cycle-1 project 2012.1.00090.S

question.value: Which multiwavelength counterparts (radio and optical-IR colour selected) can be identified for SCUBA-2 850 um sources in UKIDSS-UDS, trained on ALMA-detected SMGs, and what are their redshift distribution and clustering?

evidence.quote: By utilising an ALMA pilot study on a subset of our bright SCUBA-2 sample as a training set
We have carried out ALMA follow-up observations at 870 $\mu$m on 30 of the brighter SCUBA-2 sources in a Cycle-1 project 2012.1.00090.S
We have carried out ALMA follow-up observations at 870 $\mu$m on 30 of the brighter SCUBA-2 sources
with a synthesized beam of $\sim$ 0$\ensuremath{''}$8 FWHM
With a median rms of $\sigma =$ 0.26 mJy beam$^{-1}$
In total we detect 1088 submillimeter sources at $\geq$ 3.5 $\sigma$
The VLA radio observations at 1.4 GHz (20 cm) were carried out by the project UDS20
Eleven-band photometry ($UBVRIzJHK$\[3.6\]\[4.5\]) was measured with 3$''$ diameter apertures

what.value: ALMA SMG catalogue (52 SMGs) from the UDS pilot

evidence.quote: the primary ALMA catalog consists of 52 SMGs detected by ALMA at $> 4\,\sigma$

what.value: photometric redshifts for the K-band parent sample

evidence.quote: Photometric redshifts ($z_{\rm photo}$) have been derived for the DR8 parent sample

what.value: ALMA data reduction and source extraction

evidence.quote: the data reduction and source extraction can be found in (cite: Simpson:2015ab)
The full data reduction steps are described fully in Geach et al. (2015 in preparation)

unstated_but_needed: ALMA calibration, imaging parameters and CASA version (deferred to Simpson et al. 2015)
ALMA catalogue positions and fluxes needed to rebuild the training set
Binning used for the f_OIRTC histograms
Photometric catalogue (Almaini et al. in prep)

analysis_steps.goal: Test radio and MIPS p-value identifications against ALMA

method.value: Corrected-Poissonian p-values; accuracy and completeness measured against 52 ALMA SMGs

evidence.quote: p=1-exp(-\pi n \theta^2)

validation.value: Accuracy and completeness compared with ALMA

evidence.quote: The main parameters we consider in the tests and the training are accuracy and completeness

method.value: MIC correlation of S850 with colours; fit f_OIRTC=1/(a+exp(-b(x-c))) per colour; weighted mean fraction cut at 0.05

evidence.quote: We therefore first model $f_{\rm OIRTC}$ as a function of color by fitting a functional form, parametrized as $1/(a + e^{-b(x-c)})$

fitting.value: chi2 fit, errors from Delta chi2=1; f_OIRTC errors from 100 Monte Carlo realisations

evidence.quote: All errors are obtained assuming $\Delta \chi^2 = 1$

validation.value: Tested on SMA sample and ALESS

evidence.quote: We test our counterpart identification technique on two independent samples that are obtained from ALMA and SMA observations.

method.value: Lognormal fit to photo-z distribution; Landy-Szalay w(theta) with integral constraint and jackknife errors

evidence.quote: we calculate the two-point autocorrelation function $w(\theta)$ using the Landy & Szalay (1993) estimator.
We then perform $\chi^2$ minimization using [\[eqn:wth\]](#eqn:wth) to find the best fit $w(\theta)_{true}$
we use the maximal information coefficient (MIC) statistics of the MINE package
the photometric redshifts are estimated using the eazy template-fitting package
we use SExtractor (cite: Bertin:1996zr) to extract sources
we expect the accuracy of these identifications to be $82\pm20$%, with a completeness of $69\pm16$%
with a median redshift of $z=2.3\pm0.1$

results_numeric.quantity: Median z corrected for unidentified sources

evidence.quote: we estimate the median redshift to be $z=2.6\pm0.1$

claims.hypothesis: Can radio plus optical-IR colours identify SMG counterparts as accurately as p-values but with higher completeness?
claims.experiment: Trained on 52 ALMA SMGs and tested on SMA and ALESS
claims.finding: The OIRTC technique complements radio identification

evidence.quote: Most importantly, the OIRTC technique complements the radio identifications in selecting SCUBA-2 sources, in a sense that OIRTC selects fainter sources.

claims.hypothesis: What is the SMG redshift distribution?
claims.finding: Median z about 2.6 after correcting for unidentified sources

evidence.quote: After accounting for the sources without any radio and/or OIRTC counterpart, we estimate the median redshift to be $z=2.6\pm0.1$ for SMGs with $S_{850} >1$ mJy.

referee_caveats_inferred: Training set is small and biased to bright sources
Photo-z and counterpart incompleteness bias against high z
ALMA is used only as a training set

missing_for_reproduction: Full ALMA catalogue and photometric catalogues not given in this paper

reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Depends on catalogues not provided here.

Most importantly, the OIRTC technique complements the radio identifications in selecting SCUBA-2 sources, in a sense that OIRTC selects fainter sources.
After accounting for the sources without any radio and/or OIRTC counterpart, we estimate the median redshift to be $z=2.6\pm0.1$ for SMGs with $S_{850} >1$ mJy.
